purpose: Check whether Chromium in the packaged Electron app exposes LoAF script attribution during a synthetic projection rebuild.

isolation.fixture: Synthetic-only profile; only projection cache/state for the 1000-message target was invalidated after a profile backup. Canonical messages and source data were retained.

switchTrace.classification: Startup initial-page request, not a user-initiated session switch.

directBrowserCheck.method: DevTools Console read-only expression: performance.getEntriesByType('long-animation-frame').map(e => ({ durationMs: e.duration, scriptCount: Array.isArray(e.scripts) ? e.scripts.length : null }))
directBrowserCheck.result: Seven buffered LoAF entries were visible; every entry had scripts.length === 0.
directBrowserCheck.conclusion: For this Electron/Chromium runtime and sample, the browser provides no script attribution data. This does not identify the source of renderer long tasks; a CPU profile with usable source maps is still required.

limitations: Synthetic canonical-only fixture has a blocked ledger gate and is not a healthy large-history sample.
The long tasks overlap startup/projection maintenance timestamps but there is no causal task association.
This is not a repeated user-switch matrix, real-history content-ready comparison, or AC-7 pass.
